instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Put them in a pot and cover with cold water by about 1 inch.
Add 1 tbsp of the salt to the water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Lower to a steady boil and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick slides into a piece with no resistance.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Chop the parsley until you have about 1/2 cup.
In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil and sherry vinegar together.
Drain the potatoes in a colander and let the steam rise off them for a minute or two.
When they're cool enough to handle, transfer the potatoes to the bowl with the dressing. Add the onion, parsley, a pinch of salt and the pepper.
Toss gently so the potatoes stay in pieces. Taste one, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve chilled or at room temperature. To pack it for lunch, keep it in a lidded container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
method_notes: Only one version could be read for this dish (Spain on a Fork, the lead, 5.0 from 1 rating), so this is a fallback lead. It is the plain Cadiz style: boiled potatoes, raw onion, parsley and a sherry vinegar and oil dressing, with no egg or tuna so it stays vegan. A search summary of other Cadiz versions agrees on dressing the potatoes while still warm and says the egg and tuna version is a separate topping. The fridge time of 3 to 4 days comes from the same site's egg and tuna version, and this plain one is written as 3 days. Honest total is 30 minutes.
